Given your preference for feedback that checks understanding before moving on, and your learning style of linking new ideas to familiar concepts, a great way to check your understanding is to try the Feynman Technique. After studying a section, try explaining the topic as if you were teaching it to someone who's never heard of it before. Focus on connecting the new concepts to things you already know – really draw those links! If you stumble or find yourself using jargon without explaining it, that's a clear sign you need to revisit the material. This approach aligns perfectly with your desire for immediate feedback and your preference for relating new information to existing knowledge.
